correctness.rationale: The stated binomidness forces three explicit generalized coefficients to be integers. For any sorted prefix the ratio R_j is strictly below the final integer R_4, and every possible next shift t satisfies R_j((t+2)/(t+1))^(4-j)>=floor(R_j)+1. This gives a finite, complete branch enumeration; exact Fraction verification yields 83, then eight, then five tuples. Independent linear solution of the last root-shift equation reproduces all 83. The other three of eight have (4,2) fractions 1440/7, 500/3 and 98/3. The five survivors are products of rising factorial / Pascal-column sequences, binomid by Shapiro Theorem 15 and product closure. Direct checks through row 80 are explicitly not substituted for the proof.

originality.rationale: Theorem 25 of Shapiro (arXiv:2302.02243, Section 4.3) classifies polynomial binomid sequences only through degree two, while Theorem 15 yields positive Pascal-column examples. Neither gives the exact five-case exclusion or the three-initial-coefficient equivalence for degree-four nonnegative integer root shifts. Caalim and Tanaka (INTEGERS 24, A53) establish an abstract binomid-index framework and finite-index extensions, not polynomial-root classifications. Targeted semantic and literature/database searches found no covering quartic result. An unindexed equivalent result remains a residual risk.
residual_risks: Equivalent quartic-root recognition theorem may exist in unindexed literature or work not captured by the inspected PDFs and searches.
The abstract binomid-index characterization is stronger as a general decision condition but does not itself state or mechanically imply the explicit uniform three-test cutoff.

value.rationale: A complete classification of a natural four-parameter integer-root subclass of the difficult polynomial-binomid problem, together with a finite three-coefficient recognition criterion, is a precise motivated structural result. The theorem distinguishes the five actual families from 78 false positives to the first divisibility test, explains the additional mixed-square factor pattern and has a full exact obstruction mechanism. It is neither a bare sample computation nor a generic closure corollary.
